- `knowledge/core-reader/SKILL.md`
- `knowledge/mod-treatment/SKILL.md`
- `knowledge/mod-populations/SKILL.md`
- `knowledge/mod-ae-emergence/SKILL.md`

4	---
5	
6	# Treatment and exposure (mod-treatment): reading notes v0
7	
8	Rendered from the decision catalog `specfirst-m1` version 1 by `specfirst run skills --write`; do not edit by hand. Read `core-reader` first: it says how to record a decision. Here, for every question of the unit: its alternatives with the statement each gives, the house default, and where documents state it.
9	
10	Questions of this unit: `trt.planned.source`, `trt.actual.source`, `trt.start.source`, `trt.end.source`, `trt.date.imputation`, `date.studyday.origin`.
11	
12	## `trt.planned.source`: Where does planned treatment come from?
13	
14	Alternatives:
15	
16	- `dm_arm` (the house default): "Planned treatment is the planned arm of the subject (DM.ARM)."
17	- `dm_armcd_map`, slots map: "Planned treatment is decoded from the planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) as follows: {map}."
18	  Meaning: A code that the list does not name gives no planned treatment.
19	
20	House default: `dm_arm`.
21	
22	The answer fixes the planned treatment label of each subject. That label names the treatment
23	columns and groups every analysis done by planned treatment.
24	
25	### Where it is stated
26	
27	- Protocol: study design and treatment arms, randomization section (the list of arms).
28	- SAP: section on treatment groups or display conventions; column headers of the table shells.
29	- Often unstated: documents name the arms in prose and do not say how the label is obtained.
30	
31	### Words to look for
32	
33	- `dm_arm`: "planned treatment is the arm assigned at randomization", "as randomized", arm
34	  names used in tables exactly as the protocol lists the arms, with no relabelling rule.
35	- `dm_armcd_map`: an explicit list or table that pairs arm codes with display labels, such as
36	  "A = Drug X 10 mg, B = Placebo" or "treatment groups will be labelled as follows". The slot
37	  `map` is that list: one code and label pair per arm, copied as written.
38	
39	### Traps
40	
41	- Choose `dm_armcd_map` only when the text gives both codes and labels. Do not invent codes
42	  from arm names, and do not shorten or reword the labels.
43	- Under the map a code that is not listed gives no planned treatment. Copy every arm, placebo
44	  included; do not add entries for screen failures or subjects not assigned.
45	- Pooled groups such as "all active" or "total" are columns (`tfl.columns.total`), not map
46	  rows. Wording on the treatment actually received belongs to `trt.actual.source`.
47	- Silent documents: use the house default `dm_arm` and cite the house standard. Do not guess
48	  a map from the data.
49	
50	## `trt.actual.source`: Where does actual treatment come from?
51

12	## `ae.start.imputation`: How are partial adverse event start dates completed?
13	
14	Alternatives:
15	
16	- `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose` (the house default): "A partial adverse event start date with a known month is completed with the first day of that month, or with the treatment start date when it falls in that month."
17	  Meaning: A date with an unknown month is not completed.
18	- `first_of_month`: "A partial adverse event start date with a known month is completed with the first day of that month."
19	  Meaning: A date with an unknown month is not completed.
20	- `not_completed`: "A partial adverse event start date is not completed and gives no analysis start date."

22	House default: `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose`.
23	
24	The completed date is the analysis start date of the event, which decides whether an event
25	with an incomplete start date counts as treatment-emergent.
26	
27	### Where it is stated
28	
29	- SAP: section on missing or partial dates, or within the adverse event section, often as a
30	  list of cases (day missing; day and month missing).
31	- Protocol: rarely.
32	- Often stated only as "imputed conservatively" or "worst case", which names no rule.
33	
34	### Words to look for
35	
36	- `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose`: "a missing day is set to the first of the month;
37	  if month and year are those of the first dose, the date of first dose is used instead".
38	- `first_of_month`: "a missing day is set to 01", "first day of the month", with no reference
39	  to the first dose.
40	- `not_completed`: "partial dates will not be imputed", "incomplete start dates stay missing".
41	
42	### Traps
43	
44	- "Not before first dose" acts only when the treatment start date falls in the month of the
45	  partial date. A partial date in an earlier month becomes the first of that month.
46	- No alternative completes a date with an unknown month. Rules that set a missing month to
47	  January, or use the first dose date within the year of first dose, are not covered; report
48	  the passage.
49	- Under `not_completed` the event has no analysis start date, and `ae.teae.start` then counts
50	  it as treatment-emergent. Not completed does not mean not treatment-emergent.
51	- Rules for end dates (last day of the month) and for medication dates are other topics.
52	- Silent documents: use the house default `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose` and cite

56	
57	Alternatives:
58	
59	- `on_or_after_first_dose_date` (the house default): "An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts on or after the treatment start date."
60	  Meaning: Dates are compared; times are ignored.
61	- `at_or_after_first_dose_time`: "An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts at or after the date and time of the first dose."
62	  Meaning: A start or a first dose collected without a time counts from 00:00 of its day.

70	
71	- SAP: adverse event section, definition of a treatment-emergent adverse event.
72	- Protocol: safety or adverse event section, sometimes the statistical section.
73	- Nearly always stated; whether dates or dates and times are compared is often left open.

94	- Silent documents: use the house default `on_or_after_first_dose_date` and cite the house

100	
101	- `no_end` (the house default): "Treatment emergence has no end date."

105	  Meaning: An event that starts on the end-of-study date is still treatment-emergent. A subject without an end-of-study date has no end.
106	
107	House default: `no_end`.
108	
109	The answer decides whether events that start long after the last dose still count as
110	treatment-emergent, and so changes the counts of every adverse event table.
111	
112	### Where it is stated
113	
114	- SAP: adverse event section, in or right after the definition of treatment-emergent.
115	- Protocol: adverse event reporting period and safety follow-up; statistical section.
116	- Often missing from the definition itself, with a follow-up period described elsewhere.
117

120	- `no_end`: a definition with a start condition only, "on or after the first dose" with no

155	- SAP: adverse event section, definition of a treatment-related or drug-related event.
156	- Protocol: adverse event section, the causality (relationship) categories the investigator
157	  chooses from; the case report form shows the exact values.
158	- The scale differs from study to study, so it must be read from the documents.

Rendered from the decision catalog `specfirst-m1` version 1 by `specfirst run skills --write`; do not edit by hand. Read `core-reader` first: it says how to record a decision. Here, for every question of the unit: its alternatives with the statement each gives, the house default, and where documents state it.

Questions of this unit: `ae.start.imputation`, `ae.teae.start`, `ae.teae.end`, `ae.related.values`.

## `ae.start.imputation`: How are partial adverse event start dates completed?

Alternatives:

- `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose` (the house default): "A partial adverse event start date with a known month is completed with the first day of that month, or with the treatment start date when it falls in that month."
  Meaning: A date with an unknown month is not completed.
- `first_of_month`: "A partial adverse event start date with a known month is completed with the first day of that month."
  Meaning: A date with an unknown month is not completed.
- `not_completed`: "A partial adverse event start date is not completed and gives no analysis start date."

House default: `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose`.

The completed date is the analysis start date of the event, which decides whether an event
with an incomplete start date counts as treatment-emergent.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: section on missing or partial dates, or within the adverse event section, often as a
  list of cases (day missing; day and month missing).
- Protocol: rarely.
- Often stated only as "imputed conservatively" or "worst case", which names no rule.

### Words to look for

- `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose`: "a missing day is set to the first of the month;
  if month and year are those of the first dose, the date of first dose is used instead".
- `first_of_month`: "a missing day is set to 01", "first day of the month", with no reference
  to the first dose.
- `not_completed`: "partial dates will not be imputed", "incomplete start dates stay missing".

### Traps

- "Not before first dose" acts only when the treatment start date falls in the month of the
  partial date. A partial date in an earlier month becomes the first of that month.
- No alternative completes a date with an unknown month. Rules that set a missing month to
  January, or use the first dose date within the year of first dose, are not covered; report
  the passage.
- Under `not_completed` the event has no analysis start date, and `ae.teae.start` then counts
  it as treatment-emergent. Not completed does not mean not treatment-emergent.
- Rules for end dates (last day of the month) and for medication dates are other topics.
- Silent documents: use the house default `first_of_month_not_before_first_dose` and cite
  the house standard.

## `ae.teae.start`: When does treatment emergence begin?

Alternatives:

- `on_or_after_first_dose_date` (the house default): "An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts on or after the treatment start date."
  Meaning: Dates are compared; times are ignored.
- `at_or_after_first_dose_time`: "An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts at or after the date and time of the first dose."
  Meaning: A start or a first dose collected without a time counts from 00:00 of its day.

House default: `on_or_after_first_dose_date`.

The answer decides whether an event on the day of the first dose counts as treatment-emergent
when its time is unknown or earlier than the dose. Every adverse event count depends on it.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: adverse event section, definition of a treatment-emergent adverse event.
- Protocol: safety or adverse event section, sometimes the statistical section.
- Nearly always stated; whether dates or dates and times are compared is often left open.

### Words to look for

- `on_or_after_first_dose_date`: "onset on or after the date of first dose", "starting on or
  after the day of first study treatment", "on or after Day 1".
- `at_or_after_first_dose_time`: "onset at or after the time of the first dose", "start date
  and time on or after the date and time of first dose", "after the first administration,
  taking the time into account".

### Traps

- "After the first dose" without a word on time does not settle dates against times. If the
  documents never mention times for this comparison, treat that question as silent.
- Under `at_or_after_first_dose_time` a start or a dose without a time counts from 00:00 of
  its day: an event on the dose day with no time is before a dose timed later that day.
- Fixed for every alternative: a subject without a treatment start date has no emergent
  events; an event that ends before the treatment start date is not emergent; an event
  without an analysis start date is emergent.
- Worsening of an event present before treatment is not part of this entry. The end of the
  emergence period is `ae.teae.end`.
- Silent documents: use the house default `on_or_after_first_dose_date` and cite the house
  standard.

## `ae.teae.end`: When does treatment emergence end?

Alternatives:

- `no_end` (the house default): "Treatment emergence has no end date."
- `last_dose_plus_days`, slots days: "Treatment emergence ends {days} days after the treatment end date."
  Meaning: An event that starts on the last day of the window is still treatment-emergent. A subject without a treatment end date has no end.
- `end_of_study`: "Treatment emergence ends at the end-of-study date."
  Meaning: An event that starts on the end-of-study date is still treatment-emergent. A subject without an end-of-study date has no end.

House default: `no_end`.

The answer decides whether events that start long after the last dose still count as
treatment-emergent, and so changes the counts of every adverse event table.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: adverse event section, in or right after the definition of treatment-emergent.
- Protocol: adverse event reporting period and safety follow-up; statistical section.
- Often missing from the definition itself, with a follow-up period described elsewhere.

### Words to look for

- `no_end`: a definition with a start condition only, "on or after the first dose" with no
  upper limit, "all events after the start of treatment".
- `last_dose_plus_days`: "up to 30 days after the last dose", "within 7 days of the last
  administration", "through N days after the end of treatment". The slot `days` is that
  number.
- `end_of_study`: "until the end of the study", "through the subject's date of study
  completion or discontinuation".

### Traps

- The limit is inclusive: an event that starts exactly N days after the treatment end date,
  or on the end-of-study date, is still treatment-emergent. "Within 30 days" gives 30.
- The window is counted from the treatment end date (`trt.end.source`), not from the last
  visit. A period in weeks converts to days (4 weeks gives 28); a period in half-lives has
  no number of days, so report the passage.
- The protocol's reporting period (how long sites collect events) is not the analysis rule.
  Use it only if the SAP defines emergence by it.
- A subject without a treatment end date, or without an end-of-study date, has no end under
  the alternative that needs that date.
- Silent documents: use the house default `no_end` and cite the house standard.

## `ae.related.values`: Which causality values count as related to study treatment?

Alternatives:

- `stated_list`, slots values: "An adverse event is related to study treatment when its causality is one of {values}."
  Meaning: The causality is the collected value of AEREL, compared exactly.

House default: none. A document states it, or it is asked.

The list decides which events count as related, as in the related row of the adverse event
summary table. An event whose causality value is not in the list is not related.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: adverse event section, definition of a treatment-related or drug-related event.
- Protocol: adverse event section, the causality (relationship) categories the investigator
  chooses from; the case report form shows the exact values.
- The scale differs from study to study, so it must be read from the documents.

### Words to look for

- `stated_list`: "related events are those assessed as possibly, probably or definitely
  related", "events with a relationship of related", "related includes ...". The slot
  `values` is the list of collected causality values that count, as the study collects them.

### Traps

- Values are compared exactly with the collected causality. Use the wording of the collected
  scale (for example POSSIBLE, not "possibly related") when the documents show it; if only
  the prose form is given, say so in the answer.
- Many SAPs count an event with missing causality as related. A list of values cannot
  express that; report the sentence with the answer.
- "Unlikely related" is the usual boundary case. Include it only if the text does.
- A two-level scale (related, not related) still needs the list; it then has one value.
- Silent documents: this entry has no house default. Do not guess from the scale;
  a person must be asked.

- `ascending_dose_placebo_first`: "placebo, then active doses from lowest to highest",
  "placebo first, followed by increasing dose", shells headed Placebo, Low Dose, High Dose.
- `protocol_order`: "in the order of the treatment arms in the protocol", "as listed in the
  study design", shells that follow the protocol's list of arms where it is not dose order.

### Traps

- "Active treatment first, then placebo" is `protocol_order` only if the protocol lists the
  arms that way. Otherwise it matches no alternative; report the passage.
- When the protocol lists placebo first and the doses ascending, both alternatives give the
  same order. Pick the one the text states.
- An active comparator has no place in a dose order. If the study has one and the text does
  not say where its column goes, report that.
- The total column is `tfl.columns.total`, not this entry.
- Silent documents: use the house default `ascending_dose_placebo_first` and cite the house
  standard.

## `tfl.columns.total`: Is there a total column?

Alternatives:

- `all_arms` (the house default): "A total column of {output} pools all treatment arms."
- `none`: "There is no total column in {output}."
- `active_arms`, slots control: "A total column of {output} pools the treatment arms other than {control}."
  Meaning: The control is named by its treatment label as the treatment columns show it.

House default: `all_arms`.

The answer decides whether the table has a last column that pools arms, and which arms it
pools. It is given once per table family.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: general conventions for tables, the section of each analysis, and the column headers
  of the table shells ("Total", "Overall", "All Active").
- Protocol: almost never.
- Often shown only by the shells, and often different for demographics and safety tables.

### Words to look for

- `all_arms`: "a total column over all treatment groups", "overall", shell column "Total".
- `none`: "by treatment group" with no total in the shell, "no total column is shown".
- `active_arms`: "all active doses combined", "pooled active", shell column "Total Active".
  The slot `control` is the label of the arm left out, as its column shows it (usually
  Placebo).

### Traps

- "Total" in a shell next to dose columns can mean all arms or all active arms; read the
  header and its footnote before choosing.
- One answer per table family: a total column in the demographics shell says nothing about
  the adverse event tables.
- A table with both a pooled active column and an overall column, or with a pooled column
  that leaves out more than one arm, matches no alternative; report the passage.
- A total column is the last column. If a shell puts it elsewhere, mention that with the
  answer.
- Silent documents: use the house default `all_arms` and cite the house standard.

## `tfl.percent.format`: How are percentages displayed?

Alternatives:

- `one_decimal_zero_blank` (the house default): "Percentages in {output} have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown without a percentage."
- `one_decimal_always`: "Percentages in {output} have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown with its percentage."

House default: `one_decimal_zero_blank`.

The answer decides what a cell with a count of zero shows: the count alone, or the count
with its percentage. It is given once per table family.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: general conventions for tables and the notes to the table shells.
- Protocol: never.
- Often unstated, or visible only in the layout of a shell.

### Words to look for

- `one_decimal_zero_blank`: "percentages are shown to one decimal place; no percentage is
  shown for a count of zero", shell cells written "0" where others are "xx (xx.x)".
- `one_decimal_always`: "percentages are shown to one decimal place" together with zero
  cells written "0 (0.0)", or "a percentage is always displayed".

### Traps

- Both alternatives have one decimal. A SAP that asks for whole-number percentages or for
  two decimals matches no alternative; report the passage.
- "One decimal place" alone does not say what happens at zero. Use the house default then,
  and say that only the decimal was stated.
- Special displays such as "<0.1" for small percentages, or "100" without a decimal, are not
  covered; report them.
- A shell is a layout sketch: "xx (xx.x)" in every cell does not prove that a zero count gets
  a percentage.
- Silent documents: use the house default `one_decimal_zero_blank` and cite the house
  standard.

## `tfl.rounding.rule`: How are displayed numbers rounded?

Alternatives:

- `half_away_from_zero` (the house default): "Displayed numbers in {output} are rounded half away from zero."
- `half_even`: "Displayed numbers in {output} are rounded half to even."

House default: `half_away_from_zero`.

The rule changes a displayed mean, percentage or other statistic only when its exact value
lies halfway between two values that can be displayed. It is given once per table family.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: general conventions for tables or for numerical precision.
- Protocol: never.
- Almost always unstated; "rounded to one decimal" says how far, not how.

### Words to look for

- `half_away_from_zero`: "conventional rounding", "a final 5 is rounded up", "rounded away
  from zero".
- `half_even`: "round half to even", "banker's rounding", "a final 5 is rounded to the
  nearest even digit".

### Traps

- For positive numbers "round half up" and half away from zero agree; for negative numbers
  such as changes from baseline they differ. Treat plain "half up" as `half_away_from_zero`
  and say so in the answer.
- A number is rounded once, from full precision to the displayed decimals. A text that
  rounds a value and then computes from the rounded value describes something else; report
  the passage.
- Truncation ("values are cut to one decimal") matches no alternative.
- The number of decimals is not decided here (`tfl.decimals.rule`, `tfl.percent.format`).
- Silent documents: use the house default `half_away_from_zero` and cite the house standard.

## `tfl.ae.summary.rows`: Which rows does the adverse event summary table have?

Alternatives:

- `standard_rows` (the house default): "The rows of the adverse event summary table are any event, related events, serious events, events leading to discontinuation of study treatment, and fatal events."
- `stated_rows`, slots rows: "The rows of the adverse event summary table are, in this order, {rows}."
  Meaning: Each row is named by its code: ANY, RELATED, SERIOUS, DISCONTINUATION or FATAL.

House default: `standard_rows`.

The answer fixes the rows of the adverse event summary (overview) table and their order.
Every row counts subjects with at least one treatment-emergent event of its kind.

### Where it is stated

- SAP: adverse event section, the sentence or list that describes the overview table.
- SAP table shells: the row labels of the summary or overview table.
- Protocol: statistical section, in general words.

### Words to look for

- `standard_rows`: exactly these five rows in this order: any event, related events, serious
  events, events leading to discontinuation of study treatment, fatal events.
- `stated_rows`: another selection or another order of those five. The slot `rows` lists
  the codes in the stated order, out of ANY, RELATED, SERIOUS, DISCONTINUATION and FATAL.

### Traps

- Only these five kinds can be rows. Severe events, serious related events, events of
  special interest or events leading to dose reduction cannot be expressed; report them with
  the answer.
- "Leading to discontinuation" means that the action taken with study treatment was
  withdrawal of the drug, not that the subject left the study.
- "Fatal" is an event that resulted in death, not the number of deaths from any cause.
- The same five rows in another order are `stated_rows`, not `standard_rows`.
- Silent documents: use the house default `standard_rows` and cite the house standard.

## 1 Synopsis

[1/p1] This protocol describes study SFRRL2UH, "A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study of MVK-215 Given Once Daily for 24 Weeks in Adults". It is a phase II trial with a parallel design, double blind, and plans to enrol 64 subjects aged 18 to 80 years.

## 2 Study design

[2/p1] Subjects are randomized to 2 arms in the ratio 1:1. The protocol lists the arms in this order:
- Arm MVK50 (Active): MVK-215 50 mg once daily; study treatment MVK-215, 50 mg per dose; 32 subjects planned.

[2/p2] The schedule of visits is SCREENING (day -14), BASELINE (day 1), WEEK 4 (day 29), WEEK 8 (day 57), WEEK 12 (day 85), WEEK 16 (day 113), WEEK 20 (day 141), WEEK 24 (day 169), and FOLLOW-UP (day 199). Unscheduled visits may take place at any time.

## 3 Study treatment

[3/p1] Study treatment is given as tablets by the oral route, once daily, and its intake is recorded on exposure records. The time of the first dose is recorded.

## 4 Assessments

### 4.1 Vital signs

[4.1/p1] Vital signs are measured as follows: Systolic Blood Pressure (SYSBP, mmHg) at every visit; Diastolic Blood Pressure (DIABP, mmHg) at every visit; Pulse Rate (PULSE, beats/min) at every visit; Weight (WEIGHT, kg) at every visit; Height (HEIGHT, cm) at SCREENING; Temperature (TEMP, C) at every visit.

### 4.3 Disposition

[4.3/p1] The end of study treatment and the end of participation in the study are each recorded as a disposition event, with the subcategories "STUDY TREATMENT" and "STUDY PARTICIPATION" respectively.

## 5 Statistical considerations

### 5.1 Analysis sets

[5.1/p1] The analyses use the randomized set, the safety set, and the efficacy-evaluable set.

[5.1/p2] The randomized set will hold every randomized subject with at least one post-baseline value of the vital sign SYSBP.

## 6 Background

[6/p1] The condition under study is a recognized health concern for which patients and clinicians continue to seek better options. This study has been designed to add careful evidence to the existing body of knowledge. The rationale draws on published literature and on earlier development work with the investigational product.

## 7 Confidentiality

[7/p1] Participant privacy will be protected throughout the study. Records will be identified by a unique code rather than by name, and access to identifiable information will be limited to authorized study personnel and regulatory representatives. Information will be handled in line with applicable data protection requirements.

1	# House standard open-default@1
2	
3	Document: house
4	Catalog: specfirst-m1 1
5	
6	This is the house standard open-default@1: an open default for analysis data and safety tables, built from public standards only.
7	
8	Each numbered statement below is a default. It holds for a study whenever the study's protocol and statistical analysis plan do not state the decision. A decision taken from this document has the status `default` and the class `house_default`, and cites the statement by its anchor, for example `doc:house#1/s1`. A line that starts with "Meaning:" repeats what the catalog says the statement means; it is not a statement of its own.
9	
10	The statements are in the standard form of the decision catalog: a parser reads each one back to its decision. Do not edit this file by hand. It is rendered from the catalog and from `house.yaml`; `specfirst gate std-1` fails when it differs.
11	
12	## 1 Treatment and exposure (mod-treatment)
13	
14	[1/s1] Planned treatment is the planned arm of the subject (DM.ARM).
15	
16	[1/s2] Actual treatment is the actual arm of the subject (DM.ACTARM).
17	
18	[1/s3] The treatment start date is the earliest start date of an exposure record with a dose.
19	
20	Meaning: An exposure record has a dose when EXDOSE is above zero, or when EXDOSE is zero and EXTRT contains PLACEBO. Which partial dates take part is decision trt.date.imputation.
21	
22	[1/s4] The treatment end date is the latest end date of an exposure record with a dose.
23	
24	Meaning: An exposure record has a dose when EXDOSE is above zero, or when EXDOSE is zero and EXTRT contains PLACEBO. Which partial dates take part is decision trt.date.imputation.
25	
26	[1/s5] A partial exposure date is not completed and is left out of the treatment dates.
27	
28	Meaning: The treatment start and end dates are taken from the exposure dates that have a year, a month and a day. A date with a missing part in the middle (a year and a day without the month) is partial.
29	
30	[1/s6] Study day 1 is the treatment start date.
31	
32	Meaning: There is no study day 0. The day before study day 1 is day -1.
33	
34	## 2 Analysis populations and disposition (mod-populations)
35	
36	[2/s1] The randomized set holds every randomized subject.
37	
38	Meaning: A subject is randomized when the planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) is present and is neither SCRNFAIL nor NOTASSGN.
39	
40	[2/s2] The safety set holds every subject who received at least one dose of study treatment.
41	
42	Meaning: A subject received a dose when the treatment start date is present. A subject is randomized when the planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) is present and is neither SCRNFAIL nor NOTASSGN; the rule of the randomized set (pop.randomized.rule) does not enter.
43	
44	[2/s3] Safety analyses group subjects by actual treatment.
45	
46	Meaning: The decision holds for every output whose analysis set is the safety set. Outputs on another analysis set group subjects by planned treatment.
47	
48	[2/s4] The end-of-study record is the disposition event record of the subject.
49	
50	Meaning: The DS record with DSCAT equal to DISPOSITION EVENT. Of several such records the last by DSSEQ is taken. The record gives the end-of-study date (its DSSTDTC) and status: COMPLETED when DSDECOD is COMPLETED, DISCONTINUED for any other term, ONGOING when the subject has no such record.
51	
52	## 3 Demographics and baseline characteristics (mod-demographics)
53	
54	[3/s1] Age groups are below 65, 65 to 80, and above 80 years.
55	
56	Meaning: The groups are labelled <65, 65-80 and >80. An age of exactly 80 is in 65-80.
57	
58	[3/s2] Race categories are shown as collected and are not pooled.
59	
60	[3/s3] Baseline weight and height are the last non-missing values on or before the treatment start date.
61	
62	Meaning: The last value is the latest by the collected date and time; of the values of one day, a value without a collected time comes before those with a time, and the highest VSSEQ breaks a remaining tie. A subject without a treatment start date has no baseline weight and height.
63	
64	[3/s4] Baseline body mass index is derived from baseline weight and height and rounded to one decimal.
65	
66	Meaning: Weight in kg divided by the square of height in m; rounding is half away from zero.
67	
68	## 4 Adverse event emergence (mod-ae-emergence)
69	
70	[4/s1] A partial adverse event start date with a known month is completed with the first day of that month, or with the treatment start date when it falls in that month.
71	
72	Meaning: A date with an unknown month is not completed.
73	
74	[4/s2] An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts on or after the treatment start date.
75	
76	Meaning: Dates are compared; times are ignored. For every alternative: an event of a subject without a treatment start date is not treatment-emergent; an event that ends before the treatment start date is not treatment-emergent; an event without an analysis start date is treatment-emergent.
77	
78	[4/s3] Treatment emergence has no end date.
79	
80	## 5 Baseline and analysis visits (mod-bds-visits)
81	
82	[5/s1] Baseline is the last non-missing value before the first dose.
83	
84	Meaning: A value is before the first dose when its date is before the treatment start date. A value on that date is before the first dose unless both its time and the time of the first dose were collected and its time is not earlier. The last value is the latest by the collected date and time; of the values of one day, a value without a collected time comes before those with a time, and the highest sequence number breaks a remaining tie. Whether records of unscheduled visits may be baseline is decision bds.unscheduled.use.
85	
86	[5/s2] Post-baseline records keep their collected visit as the analysis visit.
87	
88	Meaning: The target day of the visit is its planned study day (VISITDY). A record of an unscheduled visit has no analysis visit. A record is post-baseline when its date is after the treatment start date.
89	
90	[5/s3] Of several records in one analysis visit, the one closest to the target day is analyzed, and the earlier one on a tie.
91	
92	Meaning: Only non-missing values compete. Earlier and later are by the collected date and time; of the values of one day, a value without a collected time comes before those with a time, and the sequence number breaks a remaining tie.
93	
94	[5/s4] Records of unscheduled visits compete for baseline and for analysis visits.
95	
96	Meaning: A visit is unscheduled when it has no planned study day (VISITDY is missing).
97	
98	[5/s5] An end-of-treatment record repeats the last non-missing post-baseline value on or before the treatment end date.
99	
100	Meaning: The record has the analysis visit End of Treatment and the derivation type LOV. A subject without a treatment end date takes the last post-baseline value.
101	
102	## 6 Table of demographic and baseline characteristics (tfl-demographics)
103	
104	[6/s1] The planned outputs include the demographics table.
105	
106	[6/s2] The analysis set of the demographics table is the randomized set.
107	
108	[6/s3] The treatment columns of the demographics table are in ascending order of dose, with placebo first.
109	
110	Meaning: Each column is headed by the treatment and the number of subjects of the analysis set in it.
111	
112	[6/s4] A total column of the demographics table pools all treatment arms.
113	
114	Meaning: A total column is the last column.
115	
116	[6/s5] Percentages in the demographics table are based on the number of subjects of the analysis set in the column.
117	
118	[6/s6] Percentages in the demographics table have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown without a percentage.
119	
120	[6/s7] Quantiles in the demographics table follow SAS definition 5, the empirical distribution function with averaging.
121	
122	[6/s8] Displayed numbers in the demographics table are rounded half away from zero.
123	
124	Meaning: A number is rounded once, from its full precision to the displayed decimals.
125	
126	[6/s9] In the demographics table, the mean and the median have one more decimal than the data, the standard deviation has two more, and the minimum and the maximum have as many as the data.
127	
128	Meaning: The decimals of the data are the largest number of decimals among the values summarized in the row. Quartiles are shown as the median is.
129	
130	[6/s10] P-values in the demographics table have three decimals, and a value below 0.001 is shown as <0.001.
131	
132	[6/s11] Continuous rows of the demographics table show n, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum.
133	
134	[6/s12] The demographics table shows no comparison between treatments.
135	
136	Meaning: A comparison adds one p-value column after the treatment columns. The analysis of variance is one-way, with treatment as the factor.
137	
138	## 7 Summary table of adverse events (tfl-ae-summary)
139	
140	[7/s1] The planned outputs include the adverse event summary table.
141	
142	[7/s2] The analysis set of the adverse event summary table is the safety set.
143	
144	[7/s3] The treatment columns of the adverse event summary table are in ascending order of dose, with placebo first.
145	
146	Meaning: Each column is headed by the treatment and the number of subjects of the analysis set in it.
147	
148	[7/s4] A total column of the adverse event summary table pools all treatment arms.
149	
150	Meaning: A total column is the last column.
151	
152	[7/s5] Percentages in the adverse event summary table have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown without a percentage.
153	
154	[7/s6] Displayed numbers in the adverse event summary table are rounded half away from zero.
155	
156	Meaning: A number is rounded once, from its full precision to the displayed decimals.
157	
158	[7/s7] The rows of the adverse event summary table are any event, related events, serious events, events leading to discontinuation of study treatment, and fatal events.
159

# House standard open-default@1

Document: house
Catalog: specfirst-m1 1

This is the house standard open-default@1: an open default for analysis data and safety tables, built from public standards only.

Each numbered statement below is a default. It holds for a study whenever the study's protocol and statistical analysis plan do not state the decision. A decision taken from this document has the status `default` and the class `house_default`, and cites the statement by its anchor, for example `doc:house#1/s1`. A line that starts with "Meaning:" repeats what the catalog says the statement means; it is not a statement of its own.

The statements are in the standard form of the decision catalog: a parser reads each one back to its decision. Do not edit this file by hand. It is rendered from the catalog and from `house.yaml`; `specfirst gate std-1` fails when it differs.

## 1 Treatment and exposure (mod-treatment)

[1/s1] Planned treatment is the planned arm of the subject (DM.ARM).

[1/s2] Actual treatment is the actual arm of the subject (DM.ACTARM).

[1/s3] The treatment start date is the earliest start date of an exposure record with a dose.

Meaning: An exposure record has a dose when EXDOSE is above zero, or when EXDOSE is zero and EXTRT contains PLACEBO. Which partial dates take part is decision trt.date.imputation.

[1/s4] The treatment end date is the latest end date of an exposure record with a dose.

Meaning: An exposure record has a dose when EXDOSE is above zero, or when EXDOSE is zero and EXTRT contains PLACEBO. Which partial dates take part is decision trt.date.imputation.

[1/s5] A partial exposure date is not completed and is left out of the treatment dates.

Meaning: The treatment start and end dates are taken from the exposure dates that have a year, a month and a day. A date with a missing part in the middle (a year and a day without the month) is partial.

[1/s6] Study day 1 is the treatment start date.

Meaning: There is no study day 0. The day before study day 1 is day -1.

## 2 Analysis populations and disposition (mod-populations)

[2/s1] The randomized set holds every randomized subject.

Meaning: A subject is randomized when the planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) is present and is neither SCRNFAIL nor NOTASSGN.

[2/s2] The safety set holds every subject who received at least one dose of study treatment.

Meaning: A subject received a dose when the treatment start date is present. A subject is randomized when the planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) is present and is neither SCRNFAIL nor NOTASSGN; the rule of the randomized set (pop.randomized.rule) does not enter.

[2/s3] Safety analyses group subjects by actual treatment.

Meaning: The decision holds for every output whose analysis set is the safety set. Outputs on another analysis set group subjects by planned treatment.

[2/s4] The end-of-study record is the disposition event record of the subject.

Meaning: The DS record with DSCAT equal to DISPOSITION EVENT. Of several such records the last by DSSEQ is taken. The record gives the end-of-study date (its DSSTDTC) and status: COMPLETED when DSDECOD is COMPLETED, DISCONTINUED for any other term, ONGOING when the subject has no such record.

## 3 Demographics and baseline characteristics (mod-demographics)

[3/s1] Age groups are below 65, 65 to 80, and above 80 years.

Meaning: The groups are labelled <65, 65-80 and >80. An age of exactly 80 is in 65-80.

[3/s2] Race categories are shown as collected and are not pooled.

[3/s3] Baseline weight and height are the last non-missing values on or before the treatment start date.

Meaning: The last value is the latest by the collected date and time; of the values of one day, a value without a collected time comes before those with a time, and the highest VSSEQ breaks a remaining tie. A subject without a treatment start date has no baseline weight and height.

[3/s4] Baseline body mass index is derived from baseline weight and height and rounded to one decimal.

Meaning: Weight in kg divided by the square of height in m; rounding is half away from zero.

## 4 Adverse event emergence (mod-ae-emergence)

[4/s1] A partial adverse event start date with a known month is completed with the first day of that month, or with the treatment start date when it falls in that month.

Meaning: A date with an unknown month is not completed.

[4/s2] An adverse event is treatment-emergent when it starts on or after the treatment start date.

Meaning: Dates are compared; times are ignored. For every alternative: an event of a subject without a treatment start date is not treatment-emergent; an event that ends before the treatment start date is not treatment-emergent; an event without an analysis start date is treatment-emergent.

[4/s3] Treatment emergence has no end date.

## 5 Baseline and analysis visits (mod-bds-visits)

[5/s1] Baseline is the last non-missing value before the first dose.

Meaning: A value is before the first dose when its date is before the treatment start date. A value on that date is before the first dose unless both its time and the time of the first dose were collected and its time is not earlier. The last value is the latest by the collected date and time; of the values of one day, a value without a collected time comes before those with a time, and the highest sequence number breaks a remaining tie. Whether records of unscheduled visits may be baseline is decision bds.unscheduled.use.

[5/s2] Post-baseline records keep their collected visit as the analysis visit.

Meaning: The target day of the visit is its planned study day (VISITDY). A record of an unscheduled visit has no analysis visit. A record is post-baseline when its date is after the treatment start date.

[5/s3] Of several records in one analysis visit, the one closest to the target day is analyzed, and the earlier one on a tie.

Meaning: Only non-missing values compete. Earlier and later are by the collected date and time; of the values of one day, a value without a collected time comes before those with a time, and the sequence number breaks a remaining tie.

[5/s4] Records of unscheduled visits compete for baseline and for analysis visits.

Meaning: A visit is unscheduled when it has no planned study day (VISITDY is missing).

[5/s5] An end-of-treatment record repeats the last non-missing post-baseline value on or before the treatment end date.

Meaning: The record has the analysis visit End of Treatment and the derivation type LOV. A subject without a treatment end date takes the last post-baseline value.

## 6 Table of demographic and baseline characteristics (tfl-demographics)

[6/s1] The planned outputs include the demographics table.

[6/s2] The analysis set of the demographics table is the randomized set.

[6/s3] The treatment columns of the demographics table are in ascending order of dose, with placebo first.

Meaning: Each column is headed by the treatment and the number of subjects of the analysis set in it.

[6/s4] A total column of the demographics table pools all treatment arms.

Meaning: A total column is the last column.

[6/s5] Percentages in the demographics table are based on the number of subjects of the analysis set in the column.

[6/s6] Percentages in the demographics table have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown without a percentage.

[6/s7] Quantiles in the demographics table follow SAS definition 5, the empirical distribution function with averaging.

[6/s8] Displayed numbers in the demographics table are rounded half away from zero.

Meaning: A number is rounded once, from its full precision to the displayed decimals.

[6/s9] In the demographics table, the mean and the median have one more decimal than the data, the standard deviation has two more, and the minimum and the maximum have as many as the data.

Meaning: The decimals of the data are the largest number of decimals among the values summarized in the row. Quartiles are shown as the median is.

[6/s10] P-values in the demographics table have three decimals, and a value below 0.001 is shown as <0.001.

[6/s11] Continuous rows of the demographics table show n, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum.

[6/s12] The demographics table shows no comparison between treatments.

Meaning: A comparison adds one p-value column after the treatment columns. The analysis of variance is one-way, with treatment as the factor.

## 7 Summary table of adverse events (tfl-ae-summary)

[7/s1] The planned outputs include the adverse event summary table.

[7/s2] The analysis set of the adverse event summary table is the safety set.

[7/s3] The treatment columns of the adverse event summary table are in ascending order of dose, with placebo first.

Meaning: Each column is headed by the treatment and the number of subjects of the analysis set in it.

[7/s4] A total column of the adverse event summary table pools all treatment arms.

Meaning: A total column is the last column.

[7/s5] Percentages in the adverse event summary table have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown without a percentage.

[7/s6] Displayed numbers in the adverse event summary table are rounded half away from zero.

Meaning: A number is rounded once, from its full precision to the displayed decimals.

[7/s7] The rows of the adverse event summary table are any event, related events, serious events, events leading to discontinuation of study treatment, and fatal events.

Meaning: Every row counts subjects with at least one treatment-emergent event of its kind. Related is decision ae.related.values; serious is AESER equal to Y; leading to discontinuation is AEACN equal to DRUG WITHDRAWN; fatal is AESDTH equal to Y.

## 8 Table of adverse events by system organ class and preferred term (tfl-ae-soc-pt)

[8/s1] The planned outputs include the adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term.

[8/s2] The analysis set of the adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term is the safety set.

[8/s3] The treatment columns of the adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term are in ascending order of dose, with placebo first.

Meaning: Each column is headed by the treatment and the number of subjects of the analysis set in it.

[8/s4] A total column of the adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term pools all treatment arms.

Meaning: A total column is the last column.

[8/s5] Percentages in the adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term have one decimal, and a count of zero is shown without a percentage.

[8/s6] Displayed numbers in the adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term are rounded half away from zero.

Meaning: A number is rounded once, from its full precision to the displayed decimals.

[8/s7] System organ classes and preferred terms are sorted alphabetically.

Meaning: Frequency is the number of subjects. Preferred terms are sorted within their system organ class.

[8/s8] Every preferred term with at least one event is shown.

[8/s9] The adverse event table by system organ class and preferred term counts subjects.

## 9 Table of vital signs by visit (tfl-vitals-by-visit)

[9/s1] The planned outputs include the vital signs table by visit.

[9/s2] The analysis set of the vital signs table by visit is the safety set.

[9/s3] The treatment columns of the vital signs table by visit are in ascending order of dose, with placebo first.

Meaning: Each column is headed by the treatment and the number of subjects of the analysis set in it.

[9/s4] A total column of the vital signs table by visit pools all treatment arms.

Meaning: A total column is the last column.

[9/s5] Quantiles in the vital signs table by visit follow SAS definition 5, the empirical distribution function with averaging.

[9/s6] Displayed numbers in the vital signs table by visit are rounded half away from zero.

Meaning: A number is rounded once, from its full precision to the displayed decimals.

[9/s7] In the vital signs table by visit, the mean and the median have one more decimal than the data, the standard deviation has two more, and the minimum and the maximum have as many as the data.

Meaning: The decimals of the data are the largest number of decimals among the values summarized in the row. Quartiles are shown as the median is.

[9/s8] The vital signs table by visit shows the observed value and the change from baseline side by side.

Meaning: Change from baseline is shown for post-baseline visits only.

## Decisions without a default

This standard sets no default for the decisions below. The study documents state them, or a person is asked. They are never guessed.

- `pop.efficacy.rule`: Who is efficacy-evaluable?
- `ae.related.values`: Which causality values count as related to study treatment?
- `tfl.demog.rows`: Which characteristics does the demographics table show, in which order?
- `tfl.vs.scope`: Which parameters and analysis visits does the vital signs table show?
